language.label: Language
schedule.cannotRecreate: A snapshot cannot be recreated: it records a state of the disk that has passed. Anything outside the policy is deleted on the next scheduled run, and macOS may reclaim more than that under disk pressure — so these figures are upper bounds, not reservations.
schedule.conflict: Another scheduled task is also taking snapshots: {{tasks}}. Two of them will double the snapshot rate and apply two different retention windows to the same set. Remove one.
schedule.flatOrThinned: Snapshots can be kept flat — everything inside the window set above — or thinned as they age: that same window, then coarser bands reaching further back. Thinning reaches months back for far fewer snapshots than keeping everything that long, because an old snapshot is wanted for the day it covers rather than the hour.
schedule.installed: Schedule installed. The first snapshot is taken immediately.
schedule.none: No schedule installed. Nothing is taking snapshots automatically.
schedule.onePerPeriod: Only one snapshot is kept per period. Any others taken in the same period — including one taken automatically when files start disappearing — are removed, and the earliest is the one kept, because it holds the most of what was there.
schedule.removed: Schedule removed. Existing snapshots were left alone.
schedule.whyNeeded: macOS only takes local snapshots on its own when Time Machine has a backup disk configured. This schedule takes them without one. It needs no password: creating and deleting snapshots goes through Time Machine's own background service.
